findings.issue_text: [BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which reports one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members renders '1/2' instead of '1/1'). On any group whose member count is an exact multiple of 50, 'next' stays enabled on the last real page; clicking it fetches offset=user_count and renders a completely empty member list as if it were a valid page.

[BUG] The public members endpoint now applies a default limit of 50 to every group, but the public group members template (group/members.hbs) gained no pagination controls, so only the first 50 members are ever fetched and rendered. Group pages for groups with more than 50 members silently lose members 51+ — previously the page listed every member of manual groups (automatic groups were capped at 200); the remaining members become unreachable from the UI.

[BUG] update now reads top-level params but still unconditionally executes group.visible = params[:visible] == "true", so a request using the old nested group:{...} payload has params[:visible] == nil and the group's visible column is silently flipped to false while the response reports success. During the deploy window (browsers still running the old admin JS that PUTs group:{name, alias_level, visible, usernames}) and for existing API clients, every group save silently hides the group and drops its name/alias_level/membership changes with a 200 response.

[BUG] update no longer branches on request.patch? nor reads params[:changes], so PATCH requests carrying changes:{add:[...], delete:[...]} return success_json without applying any membership change. Existing automation that managed membership through the PATCH endpoint silently stops working — it keeps receiving 200 responses while group membership never changes, and PATCHes against automatic groups now return 200 instead of the old 403 InvalidAccess.

[BUG] findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, offset), which permits offset == user_count — a page past the last member — instead of capping at user_count - limit. Removing the last member while the final page holds exactly one member (e.g. a 51-member group on page 2) reloads with offset still at 50 against a new total of 50, leaving the admin staring at an empty '2/2' member list until they manually click 'previous'.

[BUG] create reads params[:name] at the top level and no longer accepts usernames, so old clients posting the nested group:{name:..., usernames:...} payload get name set to '' and no initial members. Existing API clients that create groups with members have their requested name and membership silently discarded — the call either fails validation on the blank name or persists an empty group, with no error indicating the payload contract changed.

[BUG] add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") without type coercion, so a request whose usernames parameter is a JSON array raises NoMethodError (undefined method `split' for Array) and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. API clients sending usernames as an array — the shape the old PATCH changes:{add:[...]} endpoint accepted — get an unhandled 500 from this admin endpoint rather than a validation error.

[BUG] findMembers builds the request URL from the live `name` property, which is two-way bound to the editable name text-field on the admin group form, so paginating or adding members after editing the name (before saving) queries a group name that does not exist. An admin who types a new name and then clicks next/previous or Add triggers GET /groups/<edited-name>/members.json, which 404s; the member list silently fails to refresh, so addMembers appears to do nothing even though the PUT succeeded.

[BUG] offset = params[:offset].to_i (and likewise limit) is passed straight into ActiveRecord's offset/limit without clamping, so a negative value such as ?offset=-1 produces 'OFFSET -1' SQL that PostgreSQL rejects with an error, returning a 500. Any client — including anonymous visitors, since this is a public endpoint — can force a 500 on a group members page with one malformed query parameter; previously the offset param was only honored for automatic groups and ignored for manual ones.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite deleted the specs that pinned the silent-skip behaviors ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users', 'succeeds silently when removing non-members') and the normal-group rename assertion, and the new .add_members/.remove_member/.update contexts only cover happy paths plus the automatic-group 422s. The silent-skip semantics are still implemented (a nil User.find_by_username result is skipped; users.delete of a non-member is a no-op) but nothing fails if a refactor turns them into errors or unexpected successes; a regression in the non-automatic rename path (group.name = params[:name] if ...) would also land untested.

[ADVISORY] The diff reshapes the public GET /groups/:name/members response into a {members, meta:{total, limit, offset}} envelope that the new frontend pagination depends on, yet no test in the diff exercises it — the only spec touched is spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, which never requests GroupsController#members. A regression in the meta envelope (a renamed key or missing total) breaks member pagination on both the admin and public group pages and would pass CI; any pre-existing spec asserting the old flat array shape would have failed and had to be updated in this diff, and none appears, so the new response contract has zero verification.

[BUG] The members action now caps every group at `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` (previously custom groups returned ALL members and automatic groups 200), but the public template group/members.hbs only got `{{#each m in members}}` — no pagination controls, route wiring, or next/previous actions were added for the public page. Any group with more than 50 members, previously fully listed on the public group page, now silently shows only the first 50 members to visitors with no way to see the rest; the admin template got a pager but the public group-members route/controller/template did not.

[BUG] totalPages computes `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`, which produces one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (100 members / 50 limit → totalPages 3 instead of 2). On the last real page showingLast is false (currentPage 2 ≠ totalPages 3), so next is enabled and navigates to offset = user_count where the server returns zero members — the admin sees an empty member list labeled '3/3' (this also triggers at exactly 50 members).

[ADVISORY] GET /groups/:name/members changed its response shape from a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to a `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` envelope, with the effective default page size dropping from 200/unlimited to 50. Out-of-tree API consumers and plugins that parse this public endpoint's response as a JSON array break silently (they receive an object and iterate nothing), with no versioning or compatibility shim in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The admin update endpoint switched from a nested `params[:group]` payload (plus the PATCH `changes[add]/[delete]` path, deleted entirely) to flat params and dropped `usernames` handling, so an old-format caller's `params[:visible]` is nil and `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` evaluates to false. Existing API consumers/scripts sending `group[visible]`, `group[usernames]`, or PATCH `changes` receive 200 success while the group's visibility is silently flipped to false and membership changes are silently dropped — the old incremental-membership API is removed with no compat path.

[ADVISORY] The members action was substantially rewritten (pagination, meta envelope, extra count query) but no spec in this diff exercises it — the test changes cover only Admin::GroupsController. Regressions in the public endpoint's limit/offset/total math or envelope shape (including the 50-member truncation above) ship unnoticed, since nothing asserts the old full-listing contract or the new meta values.

[ADVISORY] addMembers leaves the user-selector populated after adding — the diff's own `// TODO: should clear the input` marks the flow as unfinished — so the just-submitted usernames stay in the input. A second click on Add (double-click, or adding a different user later) silently re-submits the stale username list to add_members, which reports success without distinguishing new adds from already-member entries, giving the admin no feedback on what actually happened.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that don't match a user (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`) and does not trim whitespace, then renders success_json regardless of how many were skipped. An admin or API caller submitting a typo'd or padded username (e.g. 'bob, jane ') gets 200 success while only some users were added, with no indication which were skipped; the diff also deleted the old tests that documented this silent-skip behavior without adding an equivalent assertion on the new endpoint.

[ADVISORY] `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` pass negative values straight into `limit(limit).offset(offset)`, and this clamping-free path now applies to every group instead of only automatic groups as before. An unauthenticated `GET /groups/<name>/members?limit=-1` (or offset=-1) produces `LIMIT -1`/`OFFSET -1` SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects, returning a 500 from a public endpoint.

[ADVISORY] removeMember and addMembers attach only `.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` with no rejection handler, and the calling controller actions catch nothing either. When the server rejects the request (422 can_not_modify_automatic, 404, 500), the admin has already confirmed via bootbox but gets no error — the dialog closes and the member list silently stays unchanged.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which reports one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50, 100, ...), advertising a final page that contains no members. For any group whose member count is divisible by 50 the admin pager shows e.g. '1/2' with next enabled; clicking next fetches offset=user_count and renders an empty member list on the phantom last page, implying members are missing.

[BUG] GET /groups/:group_id/members changes its response from a top-level JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects to a {members, meta} envelope with no versioning, breaking every existing consumer that reads the response as an array. External API consumers and scripts iterating the old array (result.map / result[0]) now receive an object and fail; additionally the effective default page drops from 200 rows (automatic groups) / unlimited (custom groups) to 50, silently truncating results for callers that do not pass limit.

[BUG] update stops reading the nested params[:group] envelope and the PATCH changes:add/delete contract, so legacy callers that PUT group[name], group[usernames] or changes have every field silently ignored while their absent params[:visible] evaluates nil == "true" and writes visible=false. An existing integration updating a group's name or membership receives 200 success_json while the rename/membership change is dropped and the group's visibility is silently disabled — corruption with a success status instead of a 4xx.

[BUG] create moves the payload from params[:group] to top-level params, so existing callers POSTing group[name] produce name='' and a validation 422, and group[usernames] is no longer read so members cannot be assigned at creation. Every existing consumer of POST /admin/groups breaks: previously working creates now return 422, and callers migrating to the new envelope get empty groups because the usernames field is silently dropped.

[ADVISORY] group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" in update coerces a JSON request body's native true to false, because Rails parses JSON params as booleans and true == "true" is false. A JSON API client sending {"visible": true} to PUT /admin/groups/:id silently disables group visibility; only form-encoded 'true' strings behave as intended.

[ADVISORY] The same params[:visible] == "true" coercion in create turns a JSON body's native true into visible=false for the newly created group. A JSON API client creating a group with visible:true gets an invisible group back with a 200 response.

[ADVISORY] create reads only name and visible and drops the alias_level that the new-group form sends via asJSON(), so the alias level selected at creation is silently discarded. An admin who sets alias_level while creating a group gets the default level; the choice only takes effect if they notice and re-edit the group afterwards.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips any username that does not match a user and still renders success_json, so a partially-applied batch is indistinguishable from a successful one. An admin who submits 'alice,bob' with a typo sees the member list reload without bob and no error anywhere; the only documentation of this behavior was the 'succeeds silently' tests this diff deletes.

[ADVISORY] remove_member deletes membership through the raw association (group.users.delete(user_id)) while add_members uses the model API (group.add), bypassing Group#remove — the sanctioned removal path the deleted update_patch code called. Any side effect later added to Group#remove (user state refresh, counter maintenance) is skipped on this path, and the codebase now carries two divergent removal mechanisms that future changes must keep in sync.

[ADVISORY] The new pagination contract accepts an unbounded limit ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no ceiling), so ?limit=10000000 still materializes and serializes every member of the group in one request. Any caller who can see the group can force a full join scan plus full serialization of all members in one request — the unbounded path this pagination was introduced to remove remains reachable.

[ADVISORY] limit and offset are passed straight to ActiveRecord with no validation, so a negative value produces LIMIT/OFFSET with a negative argument that PostgreSQL rejects, turning the request into a 500. An API caller passing offset=-1 gets a 500 instead of a 4xx or a clamped result; the JS client clamps offsets but the endpoint itself does not.

[ADVISORY] The members action is rewritten (new envelope, limit/offset pagination, meta block) with no spec in this diff, and any pre-existing spec would fail on the shape change, so the endpoint ships untested. A regression in the offset math, the meta echo, or the envelope lands silently; the pagination contract the new client code depends on has no guard.

[ADVISORY] findMembers applies whichever response arrives last via setProperties with no request sequencing or cancellation, so overlapping pagination fetches can resolve out of order and overwrite newer offset/members state with older. Rapid next/previous clicks, or a removeMember reload racing a page change, can leave the pager showing one page's member list under another page's indicator until the next interaction re-syncs.

[ADVISORY] With create and update no longer assigning group.usernames, the Group model's usernames= full-list membership sync keeps no caller on the HTTP surface, leaving two parallel membership mechanisms — the dead model-level sync and the new add_members/remove_member endpoints. The usernames accessor and its sync callback become dead machinery the next contributor must discover is unused before changing membership semantics, and it silently rots instead of being deleted.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, which reports one page too many whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members at limit 50 yields totalPages 2 instead of 1). An admin opening a group with exactly 50, 100, or 150 members sees '1/2' with the next arrow enabled; clicking next fetches offset=limit, renders an empty member list labeled '2/2', and only the back arrow escapes the phantom page.

[BUG] The rewritten members endpoint applies the 50-member default limit to every group, whereas the old code returned the full member list for custom groups (and 200 for automatic groups), and the public group members template gained no pagination controls to compensate. Users visiting a group page with more than 50 members now see an arbitrarily truncated member list with no way to view the rest — a silent public-facing regression for every group above 50 members, including large automatic groups that previously showed up to 200.

[BUG] PATCH requests to /admin/groups/:id are no longer rejected or handled: with update_patch removed, a PATCH carrying the old changes:{add:...} payload falls through to the PUT logic where params[:visible] is nil, so group.visible is force-set to false, the membership change is silently dropped, and a 200 success_json is returned. Any client still using the incremental PATCH membership API silently makes its groups invisible in the database while believing the call succeeded — a silent data mutation answered with success.

[ADVISORY] The public GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a bare serialized array to a {members: [...], meta: {...}} envelope with no versioning or compatibility period. Out-of-tree API consumers and scripts parsing the old array response read result[0].username off an object and get undefined, producing empty or incorrect output under a 200 status.

[ADVISORY] The admin create/update payload contract was silently reshaped: nested group[name]/group[alias_level]/group[visible]/group[usernames] parameters are now ignored in favor of flat params, and the usernames parameter (initial membership at creation, full-list sync on update) was dropped entirely. An old-shape PUT that only meant to change alias_level returns 200 while ignoring the alias change and flipping visible to false (params[:visible] is nil), and an old-shape POST never applies the requested members — external API consumers break with no deprecation signal.

[ADVISORY] remove_member deletes the join row via the raw group.users.delete(user_id) association call instead of the Group#remove model method the removed PATCH flow used, so membership removal no longer shares a code path with the rest of the codebase. If GroupUser maintains group.user_count in create/destroy callbacks — the value the admin UI's member count display and new pagination arithmetic depend on — the association-level delete skips that bookkeeping and user_count drifts from real membership until the next add.

[ADVISORY] removeMember refetches with the unchanged offset, and findMembers clamps offset against the pre-fetch user_count, so removing the only member on the last page leaves the UI parked on an out-of-range offset. An admin who deletes the last member shown on the final page gets an empty member list (e.g. '2/2' with zero rows) after confirming, and must click 'previous' to see the remaining members.

[ADVISORY] addMembers ships with the acknowledged 'TODO: should clear the input' — the user-selector retains the just-added usernames after the Add action succeeds. The next Add click re-submits the previous usernames along with any new ones (e.g. 'alice,bob' when only bob was intended), so every subsequent add carries stale members whose re-addition is either a silent no-op or a server error depending on Group#add's dedup behavior.

[ADVISORY] The members action was rewritten around a new response envelope and meta-based pagination, but no spec in this diff exercises it — the specs added here cover only the admin controller actions. A regression in the envelope keys, meta.total, or the limit/offset arithmetic would silently break both the public group members page and the admin member pager with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] limit and offset are cast with to_i and passed straight into limit()/offset() with no lower bound, and the rewrite extends this exposure from automatic-only groups to every group. GET /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 (or limit=-1) produces negative OFFSET/LIMIT SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects, turning a malformed query string into a 500 on any group's public members page.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public members endpoint applies no upper bound to the user-controlled `limit` param — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is passed straight to `.limit(limit)` — so one request can force serialization of a group's entire membership. Any caller who passes the group-visibility check (including anonymous users for visible automatic groups such as trust_level_0, which contains every user) can send ?limit=999999999 and pull the full member list — every username, name, avatar and last_seen row — in a single response, making bulk user enumeration and response-size/resource amplification trivial. The pre-existing code had the same hole (custom groups dumped all members with no pagination at all), so this is not a regression, but this rewrite of the exact lines governing request size was the point to clamp limit (e.g., max 1000) and it didn't.

[ADVISORY] `add_members` calls `usernames.split(",")` directly on `params.require(:usernames)` with no type coercion, so a request whose usernames param arrives as an array or hash (the natural JSON encoding for a list field) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. An admin API client sending {"usernames": ["alice","bob"]} — or any non-string value — to this newly introduced endpoint gets an unhandled NoMethodError (500 plus a stack trace in the error stream) rather than a validation error; `params[:usernames].to_s.split(",")` (or Array() wrapping) is the one-line fix. The shipped Ember client always sends a comma-joined string, so the defect is latent until any other consumer hits the endpoint.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which returns 2 whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the 50-member limit, advertising a page that does not exist; the correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count / limit). An admin opening a group with exactly 50 (or 100, ...) members sees '1/2' with the next arrow enabled; clicking next fetches offset=50, the server returns zero members, and the member list renders empty on page 2/2.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten .update context contains a single test that only exercises automatic group id 1, so the true branch of the new guard `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` — renaming an ordinary group — has zero coverage, while the old 'is able to update group members' test that verified a normal-group rename was deleted in this same diff. A regression that stops persisting name (or visible/alias_level) for non-automatic groups passes CI; the sole update test asserts group 1's name is NOT 'WAT', which cannot detect a broken rename path for the groups admins actually edit.

[ADVISORY] This diff deletes the 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' and 'succeeds silently when removing non-members' tests, but the replacement add_members/remove_member actions retain the silent-skip behavior with no replacement assertion anywhere in the rewritten spec (the only test file changed for this controller). add_members still skips unknown usernames without error (and now also silently skips whitespace-padded entries because usernames.split(',') is never stripped) and remove_member no-ops on a non-member user_id; nothing pins that contract, so a future change to 422 on unknown users — or a bug that silently drops real members — ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test drives remove_member with xhr :put even though config/routes.rb wires the action as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the suite only ever exercises the action under a verb the route never delivers. Controller specs bypass routing so the test stays green, but a verb-wiring regression on the members DELETE route would leave every admin remove-member click failing with a routing error while this spec still passes — notable because this same controller previously branched on request.patch?, so verb-sensitive handling is real here.

[ADVISORY] Three new tests hard-code id 1 / group_id: 1 (the .update test anchored here, plus the 'cannot add members' and 'cannot remove members' examples) and depend on seeded automatic groups instead of fabricating one the way the sibling .destroy test does with Fabricate(:group, automatic: true). The 422 assertions verify test-database seed state as much as controller behavior: if automatic groups are not created before these examples run, or their ids shift, Group.find(1) raises RecordNotFound or a non-automatic group 1 fails the assertions with diagnostics unrelated to the code under test.

[ADVISORY] update drops the request.patch? dispatch, so PATCH /admin/groups/:id — which previously returned 403 for automatic groups (update_patch raised Discourse::InvalidAccess) and performed incremental membership changes via params[:changes] — is now processed as a plain PUT, and the rewritten spec contains no PATCH example. API clients that PATCH an automatic group now get 200 while visible/alias_level are mutated where they previously got 403, and PATCHes carrying changes: {add: ..., delete: ...} are silently ignored; the deleted 'cannot patch automatic groups' test was the only coverage of this surface and nothing replaces it.

[ADVISORY] The assertion group.visible.should == true in the automatic-group update test cannot fail, because groups default to visible=true — the .index test in this same diff shows a freshly built-and-saved group serializes visible: true without ever setting it — so it verifies nothing about update persisting visible. If the params[:visible] assignment in Admin::GroupsController#update is ever dropped or broken, this test still passes and the regression ships; only the name assertion in the example carries any weight.

[ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component template now ships a bare <input type="text"> with no value binding, action, or autocomplete wiring, replacing a template that previously rendered nothing. Wherever {{admin-group-selector}} is rendered, an admin gets a text field that ignores everything typed into it — dead UI shipped with no wiring anywhere in this change.

[BUG] The group write contract was changed in a single step with no expand/contract window: the nested `group[...]` payload and the PATCH `changes` membership API were removed and replaced by flat top-level params plus new /members endpoints, so an old-contract PUT/PATCH reaches `update` with `params[:visible]` nil and `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` silently persists visible=false. Admins running cached pre-deploy JS (long-lived admin tabs) and any API consumer still sending the old nested PUT payload or the removed PATCH `changes` request get a 200 success_json while the group's visible flag is silently overwritten to false and the requested rename/membership changes are dropped — and rolling back the deploy does not restore the flipped flags. In the reverse direction during a rolling deploy, new JS against old pods gets 500s (`params[:group][:name]` on nil in create/update_put) and 404s on the new /members routes, so old and new clients cannot both work against the same backend at any point in the rollout.

[ADVISORY] The public GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a bare serialized array to `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` in the same step that the client was switched to the new shape, with no versioning or compatibility window on a publicly reachable endpoint. Third-party API consumers parsing the old array shape break against the new server, and stale cached public JS (the previous findMembers' `result.map(...)`) throws a TypeError on the object response, leaving the group members page empty; conversely, new JS against not-yet-updated pods throws on `result.meta.total` — the same rolling-deploy skew as the admin endpoints, but on a route reachable by external consumers.

[BUG] The removeMember action invokes self.get("model").removeMember(member) inside the bootbox callback without returning or catching the promise, so the DELETE request has no rejection handler anywhere on the path. An admin confirms the removal, the dialog closes, and if the request fails (network error, server 500) the member silently stays in the group with no error message — the admin believes the member was removed when the operation never happened.

[BUG] The addMembers action fires this.get("model").addMembers(...) without returning or catching the promise, and never clears the usernames input (the in-code TODO), so a failed PUT is swallowed and the stale names remain in the field. An admin clicks Add, the request fails (network error/500), nothing is added and no error is shown; the input still holds the old names so the next click silently re-submits the same list, compounding the invisible failure.

[BUG] members now applies the 50-row limit to every group (the old code returned the full member list for non-automatic groups and 200 for automatic ones), while the public members template only switched to iterating `members` and gained no pagination controls. The public group members page silently shows only the first 50 members of any larger group — no pager, no total — presenting a truncated list as complete; every non-automatic group that previously listed all members regresses, and visitors have no way to see the rest.

[BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that do not resolve — `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` has no else branch and the split names are not stripped — then renders success_json regardless. An admin who types a typo'd, whitespace-padded, or recently-deleted username into the user-selector gets a 200 success response, no member is added, and nothing indicates which names were dropped — the API reports success while dropping the requested work.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members with limit 50 yields totalPages = 2). For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of 50 the pager shows a phantom last page with next enabled; clicking it fetches offset == user_count, the server returns zero members, and the admin is left staring at an empty member list labeled e.g. 2/2 (findMembers' Math.min(user_count, offset) clamp preserves the empty offset).

[BUG] next/previous commit group.set("offset", offset) before findMembers() resolves, with no rollback on failure and no in-flight guard, so pagination bookkeeping is updated for requests that may fail or complete out of order. A failed page fetch leaves the page label advanced while the list still shows the previous page, and the next click silently skips a page; two rapid clicks issue overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses overwrite the newer page with older members because setProperties runs whenever a response lands.

[BUG] members passes params[:offset].to_i and (params[:limit] || 50).to_i straight into .offset()/.limit() with no validation, so negative values reach SQL as OFFSET -1 / LIMIT -1. GET /groups/{name}/members.json?offset=-1 makes PostgreSQL raise its 'must not be negative' error as ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and the request returns a raw 500 instead of a 4xx for the malformed parameter.

[BUG] removeMember's .then calls self.findMembers() without returning it, so the outer promise resolves before the reload starts and the reload's rejection is detached from the chain. After a successful DELETE, if the member-list refresh fails the UI keeps displaying the removed member as a current member with no error surfaced anywhere.

[BUG] addMembers has the same defect: the .then calls self.findMembers() without returning it, detaching the reload's failure from the promise chain. After a successful add, a failed refresh leaves the newly added member invisible in the list with no error, so the admin cannot tell whether the add took effect.

[BUG] create only assigns name and visible — the alias_level that the client's asJSON() sends is ignored, unlike update which assigns params[:alias_level]. The new-group form renders the alias-level combo-box unconditionally, so an admin who picks a level before the first save gets it silently dropped (group created with the default) while the form keeps displaying the chosen value until the next save.

[ADVISORY] setupController fires model.findMembers() fire-and-forget with no rejection handler; the old afterModel returned the promise, so a fetch failure aborted the transition and surfaced, while the new code discards it. If the members fetch fails, the admin group page renders an empty member list with no error — indistinguishable from an empty group — a regression in error visibility for the admin members view.

[ADVISORY] Same fire-and-forget model.findMembers() in the public group-members route's setupController with no rejection handler. A failed members fetch renders the public group members page as an empty table with no error, silently telling visitors the group has no members.

[ADVISORY] limit is read from params with no upper bound, so a single request can demand unbounded serialization of a group's membership. ?limit=1000000 on the public members endpoint serializes an entire group in one response — for automatic groups like trust_level_0 that is every user on the forum — letting any caller (including anonymous visitors for visible groups) generate arbitrarily large responses at will.

[ADVISORY] add_members performs no membership check before group.add(user), so re-adding a username that is already a member inserts a second group_users row, which violates the table's unique (group_id, user_id) index and 500s the request. The user-selector offers existing members for selection, so an admin re-adding one triggers the failure; combined with the client's missing rejection handler the 500 is swallowed and the Add button appears to do nothing.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific branch in Admin::GroupsController#update (old request.patch? -> update_patch/update_put). Because Rails still routes PATCH /admin/groups/:id to #update, PATCH requests that previously hit update_patch (raising Discourse::InvalidAccess for automatic groups and applying changes[:add]/[:delete]) will now return success and silently ignore changes payloads. The spec also deletes the only PATCH coverage (“cannot patch automatic groups”) without replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The assertion group.visible.should == true in the automatic-group update test cannot fail, because groups default to visible=true — the .index test in this same diff shows a freshly built-and-saved group serializes visible: true without ever setting it — so it verifies nothing about update persisting visible. If the params[:visible] assignment in Admin::GroupsController#update is ever dropped or broken, this test still passes and the regression ships; only the name assertion in the example carries any weight.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a spec `context ".update"` that does `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, name: "WAT", visible: "true"` and then asserts `group.visible.should == true`. From the diff we can see other tests expect a newly-created group to serialize with `"visible"=>true` without ever explicitly setting it (the `.index` spec builds/saves a group and expects `visible: true`). Given that, the `.update` test’s `visible == true` assertion is likely redundant and may not actually validate that `Admin::GroupsController#update`’s `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` line is doing anything (it would still pass if the group was already visible by default / pre-seeded). This is a test-quality gap rather than an app defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component template now ships a bare <input type="text"> with no value binding, action, or autocomplete wiring, replacing a template that previously rendered nothing. Wherever {{admin-group-selector}} is rendered, an admin gets a text field that ignores everything typed into it — dead UI shipped with no wiring anywhere in this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/admin-group-selector.hbs` only removes surrounding blank lines; it already contained exactly `<input type="text">` before and still does after. There is no change introducing a new, unwired input field, nor did it previously “render nothing.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The group write contract was changed in a single step with no expand/contract window: the nested `group[...]` payload and the PATCH `changes` membership API were removed and replaced by flat top-level params plus new /members endpoints, so an old-contract PUT/PATCH reaches `update` with `params[:visible]` nil and `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` silently persists visible=false. Admins running cached pre-deploy JS (long-lived admin tabs) and any API consumer still sending the old nested PUT payload or the removed PATCH `changes` request get a 200 success_json while the group's visible flag is silently overwritten to false and the requested rename/membership changes are dropped — and rolling back the deploy does not restore the flipped flags. In the reverse direction during a rolling deploy, new JS against old pods gets 500s (`params[:group][:name]` on nil in create/update_put) and 404s on the new /members routes, so old and new clients cannot both work against the same backend at any point in the rollout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the old nested write contract and PATCH membership API: `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` (not `params[:group]`), and `update` now sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` and `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic`, with no handling for `params[:group]` or PATCH `changes`. An old client still sending `group[visible]`/`group[name]` (or PATCH `changes`) will reach `update` with `params[:visible]` nil, causing `visible` to be persisted as `false` and returning `success_json` if save succeeds, while rename/membership updates are dropped. This silent flag flip/data loss is directly implied by the new param access patterns in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from a bare serialized array to `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` in the same step that the client was switched to the new shape, with no versioning or compatibility window on a publicly reachable endpoint. Third-party API consumers parsing the old array shape break against the new server, and stale cached public JS (the previous findMembers' `result.map(...)`) throws a TypeError on the object response, leaving the group members page empty; conversely, new JS against not-yet-updated pods throws on `result.meta.total` — the same rolling-deploy skew as the admin endpoints, but on a route reachable by external consumers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public `GroupsController#members` response from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (object wrapper). At the same time, the client `Discourse.Group#findMembers` switches from `result.map(...)` to expecting `result.meta.*` and `result.members`. This creates an immediate incompatibility: old JS against new server will throw (`result.map` on an object), and new JS against old server will throw (`result.meta` undefined). The diff shows no versioning, backward-compatible response, or compatibility window, so both third-party consumers of the endpoint and rolling-deploy asset skew can break group members pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The removeMember action invokes self.get("model").removeMember(member) inside the bootbox callback without returning or catching the promise, so the DELETE request has no rejection handler anywhere on the path. An admin confirms the removal, the dialog closes, and if the request fails (network error, server 500) the member silently stays in the group with no error message — the admin believes the member was removed when the operation never happened.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `removeMember` action calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` inside the `bootbox.confirm` callback without returning the promise or attaching any `.then/.catch` (or equivalent). The model method `Discourse.Group.removeMember` returns the `Discourse.ajax(... DELETE ...)` promise and only refreshes members on success (`.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })`), but there is no failure handling in the action path shown in the diff. This is a concrete robustness/UX gap introduced by the new remove-member flow, though the UI will still show the member if the request fails (so it’s not a clearly broken state), just without an explicit error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The addMembers action fires this.get("model").addMembers(...) without returning or catching the promise, and never clears the usernames input (the in-code TODO), so a failed PUT is swallowed and the stale names remain in the field. An admin clicks Add, the request fails (network error/500), nothing is added and no error is shown; the input still holds the old names so the next click silently re-submits the same list, compounding the invisible failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and has a `// TODO: should clear the input`, but it neither clears `usernames` nor returns the AJAX promise (`Group#addMembers` returns a `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise). The stale input aspect is directly confirmed by the TODO and lack of any `this.set("usernames", ...)`. However, the claim that a failed PUT is "swallowed" / "no error is shown" is not provable from the diff alone because global AJAX error handling may exist elsewhere; the diff only shows absence of local handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] members now applies the 50-row limit to every group (the old code returned the full member list for non-automatic groups and 200 for automatic ones), while the public members template only switched to iterating `members` and gained no pagination controls. The public group members page silently shows only the first 50 members of any larger group — no pager, no total — presenting a truncated list as complete; every non-automatic group that previously listed all members regresses, and visitors have no way to see the rest.

adjudication.rationale: Verified by the diff: `GroupsController#members` now always paginates with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for *all* groups (removed the old `if group.automatic?` block that previously only limited automatic groups and used a 200 default). On the public side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()` (which hits `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset`), and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` without adding any pagination UI/controls. With default `Discourse.Group` `limit: 50, offset: 0`, the public members page will only show the first 50 members for any larger group, with no way to navigate to the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that do not resolve — `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` has no else branch and the split names are not stripped — then renders success_json regardless. An admin who types a typo'd, whitespace-padded, or recently-deleted username into the user-selector gets a 200 success response, no member is added, and nothing indicates which names were dropped — the API reports success while dropping the requested work.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user, with no `else`/error reporting. It also does not `strip` each split token, so whitespace-padded usernames won’t resolve. Despite skipped/invalid usernames, it still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it will even if no members were added), so the API can report success while dropping requested additions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members with limit 50 yields totalPages = 2). For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of 50 the pager shows a phantom last page with next enabled; clicking it fetches offset == user_count, the server returns zero members, and the admin is left staring at an empty member list labeled e.g. 2/2 (findMembers' Math.min(user_count, offset) clamp preserves the empty offset).

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). This overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50/50 => 2 pages). The `next` action sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so for 50 members it will advance `offset` from 0 to 50. Then `findMembers()` (in `discourse/models/group.js`) clamps `offset` with `Math.min(user_count, ...)`, preserving `offset == user_count`, and the server `/groups/:name/members.json` returns an empty `members` list for `offset == total`. This produces the phantom last page behavior described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] next/previous commit group.set("offset", offset) before findMembers() resolves, with no rollback on failure and no in-flight guard, so pagination bookkeeping is updated for requests that may fail or complete out of order. A failed page fetch leaves the page label advanced while the list still shows the previous page, and the next click silently skips a page; two rapid clicks issue overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses overwrite the newer page with older members because setProperties runs whenever a response lands.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` actions `next`/`previous` set `group.offset` immediately (`group.set("offset", offset)`) and then call `group.findMembers()`. `currentPage`/`showingFirst`/`showingLast` are computed from `offset`, so the page label/navigation state updates even if the AJAX in `findMembers` fails (no `.catch`/rollback) and `members` remains unchanged because `members` is only set inside the `.then` in `findMembers` (group model). Also, there is no in-flight request guard/cancellation: multiple rapid clicks will issue overlapping `Discourse.ajax` calls, and whichever response returns last will run `self.setProperties({ ... members: ... })`, potentially overwriting a newer page with an older response. This matches the reported inconsistent pagination/bookkeeping behavior and is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] members passes params[:offset].to_i and (params[:limit] || 50).to_i straight into .offset()/.limit() with no validation, so negative values reach SQL as OFFSET -1 / LIMIT -1. GET /groups/{name}/members.json?offset=-1 makes PostgreSQL raise its 'must not be negative' error as ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and the request returns a raw 500 instead of a 4xx for the malformed parameter.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then directly calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no guard against negative values, so `offset=-1` becomes `OFFSET -1` in SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects (raising an exception and likely producing a 500). This behavior is newly applied to all groups (previously pagination was only applied for `group.automatic?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] removeMember's .then calls self.findMembers() without returning it, so the outer promise resolves before the reload starts and the reload's rejection is detached from the chain. After a successful DELETE, if the member-list refresh fails the UI keeps displaying the removed member as a current member with no error surfaced anywhere.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core problem: `findMembers()` became asynchronous and is being invoked without being properly handled/awaited/returned. The candidate specifies the concrete manifestation in `removeMember()`—calling `self.findMembers()` inside `.then` without returning it—causing the outer promise to resolve early and detaching failures, which is a race/ordering issue consistent with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] addMembers has the same defect: the .then calls self.findMembers() without returning it, detaching the reload's failure from the promise chain. After a successful add, a failed refresh leaves the newly added member invisible in the list with no error, so the admin cannot tell whether the add took effect.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `addMembers` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` but does not `return self.findMembers()` from the `then` callback. That means the promise returned by `addMembers()` resolves as soon as the PUT succeeds, regardless of whether the subsequent `findMembers()` reload fails. The same pattern exists in `removeMember`. This matches the finding: a failed refresh would not be surfaced through the promise chain and could leave the UI showing stale members without an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create only assigns name and visible — the alias_level that the client's asJSON() sends is ignored, unlike update which assigns params[:alias_level]. The new-group form renders the alias-level combo-box unconditionally, so an admin who picks a level before the first save gets it silently dropped (group created with the default) while the form keeps displaying the chosen value until the next save.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` the client now POSTs `{ name, alias_level, visible }`, and the new-group form always renders the alias-level `combo-box` (`admin/templates/group.hbs`), so a user can choose `alias_level` before first save. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`, while `#update` does (`group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i ...`). Additionally, the client `create()` only sets `id` from the response (`self.set('id', resp.basic_group.id);`), so the UI can keep showing the pre-selected `alias_level` even though the server created the group with the default alias level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupController fires model.findMembers() fire-and-forget with no rejection handler; the old afterModel returned the promise, so a fetch failure aborted the transition and surfaced, while the new code discards it. If the members fetch fails, the admin group page renders an empty member list with no error — indistinguishable from an empty group — a regression in error visibility for the admin members view.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the routes’ `afterModel` hooks that returned `model.findMembers()` (e.g. `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`) and replaces them with `setupController(...){ controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers(); }`, which does not return/chain the promise and has no rejection handling. Since `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and no `.catch`, a request failure will no longer reject the transition or surface via the route hook; the page will render with `members` unset/empty (templates iterate `{{each ... in members}}`), making failures indistinguishable from an empty group. This is a real behavior regression introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Same fire-and-forget model.findMembers() in the public group-members route's setupController with no rejection handler. A failed members fetch renders the public group members page as an empty table with no error, silently telling visitors the group has no members.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, `setupController` now calls `model.findMembers();` as fire-and-forget and does not return/chain the promise or handle rejection. `findMembers()` performs an Ajax request and only sets `members` on success. The template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, so if the request fails (or never resolves), `members` remains unset and the page will render no rows with no route-level error handling triggered by the returned promise (since nothing is returned from `setupController`). This is a diff-grounded behavior regression compared to the prior `afterModel` that returned the promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] limit is read from params with no upper bound, so a single request can demand unbounded serialization of a group's membership. ?limit=1000000 on the public members endpoint serializes an entire group in one response — for automatic groups like trust_level_0 that is every user on the forum — letting any caller (including anonymous visitors for visible groups) generate arbitrarily large responses at will.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit)` with no upper bound. This makes the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint capable of returning arbitrarily large member lists (and serializing them) when a caller supplies a huge `?limit=` value. The prior logic only applied pagination to automatic groups and defaulted to 200; the new code enables large limits for all groups without a cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] add_members performs no membership check before group.add(user), so re-adding a username that is already a member inserts a second group_users row, which violates the table's unique (group_id, user_id) index and 500s the request. The user-selector offers existing members for selection, so an admin re-adding one triggers the failure; combined with the client's missing rejection handler the 500 is swallowed and the Add button appears to do nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows usernames are split and each resolved user is blindly added via `group.add(user)` with no explicit check for existing membership (`user` already in `group.users`). Whether this actually 500s depends on `Group#add` / association behavior and DB constraints, which are not shown in the diff, so the finding’s claim of a guaranteed unique-index violation and 500 cannot be fully verified. However, the lack of an explicit guard in the new endpoint is a concrete, diff-grounded edge case risk introduced by this change. The client also does not attach any error handling to the promise returned by `model.addMembers(...)` in the new `addMembers` action, so failures could be silent at the UI level.
